To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Neisseria Ig A1 protease associated α‐prote in s are transported into the nuclei of human primary cells and that they share several structural features with eukayotic transcription factors.
the neisserial α-proteins are functional transcription factor-like proteins that enter human cells and are transported into the nuclei, where they accumulate in the nucleoli.
the α‐protein component of the Neisseria Ig‐A1 protease is capable of entering certain primary human cells via an endocytic pathway and accumulating in the nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel mechanisms of host cell invasion by bacterial pathogens.
the identification of novel pathogenicity factors in Neisseria species.
the characterization of a novel class of virulence factors of pathogenic neisserial species, which may have implications for the development of new therapeutic strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
α‐protease may have multiple functions, which include the regulation of host cell functions and the transport of IgA1‐protease into human cells.
the neisserial α proteins are not only involved in the processing of IgA1, they also may have a regulatory function in the human cell.
Neisseria species secrete a protein which has the potential to enter the nucleus of host cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the α‐protein is an important factor in the interaction of the pathogenic Neisseria with their hosts.
Neisseria species are equipped with an IgA1‐degrading enzyme and with a factor that may be able to interfere with the host‐cell transcriptional machinery.
Neisseria spp. are able to manipulate host cells in several ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Neisseria species are able to target the host cell nucleus with a factor that is covalently connected to the virulence factor IgA1 proteases.
Neisseria Ig A1 protease-associated α-proteins are capable to enter the nuclei of human primary cells.
